38. Moreover, the Counc il is clear that if intoxication is regarded as an aggravating
factor in a case this does not in any way rule out the possibility of a court adopting,
in its sentence, a problem -solving approach to address the underlying cause or
causes of offending behavi our, thus reducing the possibility of re -offending and
contributing to the protection of the public.

39. Nor, in the Council’s view, is the guideline’s treatment of intoxication as a possible
aggravating factor incompatible with listing a willingness to “addr ess… any drug
(or) alcohol issues” as a possible mitigating factor. Self -administered intoxication
and a willingness to address drug or alcohol issues can co-exist in a case, and
courts remain free to balance their presence when deciding on the most
appropriate sentence.
